dispositions_summary.method: The automatic families first printed in 1781 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 653 items printed somewhere, 245 in 4 or more catalogue series by the finder's count), and the families of 1780 were looked for on the 1781 pages (items_from_1780.json: 45 items, 5 in 4 or more). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by machine by about 100 words of its text from the finder's position, over all 1,623 pages in both transcriptions (a dense run of its word 5-grams, at least a quarter of them); the counts were joined into documents (items standing together on most of the same pages). The admitted and chosen items were counted again by about 70 words from their own opening (counts_1781.json), and the pages that only quote or recite them were read and left out. Each admitted printing was checked against its page scan.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted by their own words and joined into documents, 181 items of 1781 are eligible: 123 in 4 papers, 43 in 5, 15 in 6. 14 items are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted; 13 more are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news; together, with their introductions and later passages, they are 36 of the eligible documents. 145 eligible items are not chosen and are listed with their counts and their own opening words. 226 more documents of the item finder are in 3 papers or fewer by their own words, below the bar (docs_1781.json); they are not listed one by one.
counted_item_by_item.Titles of the items not chosen: Each eligible item not chosen is listed by its own words: the dateline or heading before the finder's position and the words that follow (some begin inside the item, where the finder's position does); a notice that names a private person is described instead.
